publishPolicy: Summaries only. No API keys, raw provider responses, project .scratch paths, or active-pack keys.

seats.name: Chair
seats.reason: Measured 78% catch / 100% precision on the one-sample pair; a two-sample repeat narrowed the gap and Qwen failed two schema checks. The binding is unchanged.

seats.name: Shape
seats.reason: Measured 91% catch / 100% precision. Qwen is 87%; GLM 5.3 was 87% on 9 of 10 at about 6.6x the cost.

seats.name: Experience
seats.reason: Measured 93% catch / 100% precision, completed 10 of 10 at 8k. GLM 5.3 completed 10 of 10 at 91% for about 25x the cost; GLM Flash was incomplete at both budgets.

seats.name: Risk
seats.reason: Measured 100% catch / 85% precision. Caught the major credential leak Qwen missed; four false claims are the accepted cost.

seats.name: Blindspot
seats.reason: Measured on ten tasks at 60% catch / 66% precision with 40 false claims. The one-task pilot was optimistic; GLM Flash is still the only model with a valid visual review.

chair.tiebreaker: Qwen's 80% vs DeepSeek's 78% is inside the rough confidence band. On Task 07 Qwen returned `new pane command list` as an option id instead of B, so the chair keeps DeepSeek. GLM Flash also failed: at 16k it returned invalid JSON on 6 of 10 tasks; at 8k it returned 7 of 10. GLM 5.3 also ran at 16k: 81% catch / 100% precision on 7 of 10 tasks; three answers hit the 16k output cap. Its all-in cost was about $0.016 per valid task, roughly 25x DeepSeek, so it did not earn a rebind.
chair.whatWouldFlip: If Qwen removes the invalid option id and keeps its catch, the chair becomes a genuine coin-flip and cost decides.
chair.stability: A two-sample repeat is a stability check: DeepSeek 77% catch / 99% precision on 20/20 records, Qwen 79% / 100% on 18/20 (two schema failures in sample 2). The earlier precision gap did not replicate, so the chair is closer than one run suggested; the binding is unchanged.

shape.tiebreaker: DeepSeek is 91% vs Qwen's 87%. The bands overlap, but DeepSeek leads on the complete runs and has no false claims. GLM Flash returned invalid JSON on 5 of 10 tasks at 16k and 2 of 10 at 8k, so it is not a complete challenger. GLM 5.3 ran at 16k: 87% catch / 100% precision on 9 of 10 tasks, below DeepSeek's 91% and about 6.6x the cost.
shape.whatWouldFlip: A complete Qwen run above 91% with 100% precision, or a DeepSeek regression below 87%.

experience.tiebreaker: DeepSeek completed all ten tasks at 93% catch / 100% precision at 8k. GLM 5.3 also completed all ten at 16k, but at 91% catch and about 25x the cost per valid task ($0.00787 vs $0.000309). The complete premium challenger did not beat the binding. GLM Flash completed 7/10 at 16k and 6/10 at 8k.
experience.whatWouldFlip: A complete challenger above 93% at a cost the user accepts, or a DeepSeek regression below 91%.

risk.tiebreaker: GLM 5.3 caught every key defect (100%) and Qwen missed the major credential exposure in Task 08. The four false claims are the accepted cost of that catch.
risk.whatWouldFlip: A Qwen run that catches the credential exposure without adding false claims, at roughly a third of the cost.

blindspot.tiebreaker: GLM Flash completed all ten tasks when one retry per task was allowed. Catch fell to 60% and precision to 66% with 40 false claims, so the one-task 73% / 100% pilot was optimistic. It remains the only model with a valid visual review.
blindspot.whatWouldFlip: A second model with a valid ten-task review, or a GLM Flash run with materially higher precision at the same catch.

covers: Synthesis of four seat proposals into an options table, a recommendation, dissent and rejected options.
Use of the proposals' option ids, including a trap that rejects an invented id.
Precision under disagreement: the chair must not hide dissent or claim consensus.
limits: Text only; it does not test whether the options are modern, beautiful or well sourced.
Ten briefs from one project; no multi-user, auth, performance or migration-scale cases.
One sample per task; confidence is medium.
GLM Flash is partial at both budgets: 4/10 valid at 16k, 7/10 at 8k. The 16k row is shown because it matches the measured budget.
GLM 5.3 is partial at 16k: 7/10 valid, 81% catch, 100% precision, at about $0.016 per valid task.

covers: The smallest viable shape, the existing seams it uses, what it defers and how to reverse it.
Whether a new dependency or a second path is proposed when a simpler seam exists.
A rollback path for storage and settings changes.
limits: It rewards the smallest shape; it does not judge whether the result is modern or pleasant.
Ten tasks from one project; no greenfield stack choice.
GLM Flash is partial at both budgets: 5/10 valid at 16k, 8/10 at 8k.
GLM 5.3 is partial at 16k: 9/10 valid, 87% catch, 100% precision, at about $0.0038 per valid task.

covers: An observable experience thesis: the three-second read, first-run path, copy voice, one good moment and the friction to avoid.
Empty, loading, error, composer, destructive confirmation, settings and first-run states.
Evidence and non-goals rather than adjective-only claims.
limits: The thesis is still an assertion; no artifact exists to score.
Beauty is tested with the one throwaway visual probe, not this seat.
DeepSeek ran at 8k; GLM 5.3 completed at 16k and GLM Flash did not complete at either budget, so the budgets differ.
One sample; confidence is medium.

covers: Ten blind code slices: SQL injection, path traversal, IDOR, JWT, SSRF, command injection, deserialization, secret leakage, crypto and config exposure.
Every key defect is listed, including the major credential leak Qwen missed.
False claims are counted, so the 100% catch is not reported without its precision cost.
limits: Small synthetic slices, not a full application or dependency audit.
Ten tasks; one sample each; confidence is medium.
The 4k rows for GLM Flash, DeepSeek and Haiku are partial and not comparable with the 16k rows.

covers: Ten screens at 375 and 900, light and dark: project list, empty, loading, error, settings, table, navigation, validation, long content and a dark dashboard.
130 keyed defects covering contrast, clipping, overlap, alignment, spacing, missing badges, colour-only status and invisible borders.
A one-to-one match between the model's finding region and the keyed defect region.
limits: The measured run allowed one retry per task; the first ten-task run completed 8 of 10.
Precision is 66% with 40 false claims, so the seat is noisy even when it completes.
It measures defect detection, not taste or beauty.
One sample; confidence is medium.

priceBasis: Prices are the declared prices carried by each run record, in USD per 1M tokens.
The council and visual runs used the min80 estimate; the risk GLM run used min80 and the risk Qwen run used list.
Measured cost per task is the run record, not a catalogue ratio.
Risk measured cost: GLM 5.3 $0.00324/task, Qwen $0.00123/task, about 2.6×. The earlier 13× claim is not supported by the declared prices or the measured cost.
The price table was fetched on 2026-11-21 from the provider catalogue.
Cost / task in the tables is the all-in evidence cost across every sample; a single council call divides by the sample count.
protocolNotes: Reasoning models need large output budgets: 1,200 and 4,000 tokens truncated JSON; 16,000 was needed for several tasks.
A fenced JSON answer is a failed task. Claude Haiku fences every answer and cannot be measured under this protocol.
One sample gives medium confidence; repeated samples give high confidence. The runner now accepts 1–5 samples.
Seat variants (#low/#high) are not tested; the harness tests base models.
The visual pack is now ten tasks and 130 keyed defects. The measured run completed 10/10 with one retry per task, at 60% catch / 66% precision and 40 false claims.
